source.paginationNote: The source has 130 physical PDF pages and 128 numbered printed pages plus cover/other unnumbered physical matter. This subreport covers only printed 43–100 / PDF44–101.

scope.cohort: All PHB Cleric, Druid, Magic-user and Illusionist spell-description article bodies, shared field/class spell notes physically on these pages, visible table/procedure/qualifier/continuation structures, and the Illusionist first-level Magic-user nested list.
scope.boundary: PHB p.100 begins the distinct general Spell Casting section. Its passage continues beyond p.100 and is not part of the 413 physical spell-description-head denominator; only the Illusionist p.100 spell list and Vision article are in this body cohort.
notIncluded: PHB spell-list tables on printed 40–42; they are a separate source unit.
The general Spell Casting procedure and scroll section beginning p.100 and continuing p.101; separate body/owner audit scope.
No source repairs or current app/data/citation edits.

method.sourceFirst: Used the independently counted physical article-head census (413 heads: Cleric76, Druid78, Magic-user194, Illusionist65) and the pagewise actual-PDF visual roster; inspected each of the 58 full-page 2x images individually with the printed folio visible. Image/candidate OCR was only a locator. Spell-body paragraphs, continuation boundaries, explicit limits and visible tables/procedures were read from page pixels.
method.siteJoin: Joined each physical head by class, level, printed page and normalized printed title to one exact PHB spell owner in the pinned full site snapshot. Compared its sourceRecord, captured detail DOM innerText/textContent and captured app-built public search document. Every route exists, route hash matches, detail root is visible, and its title query returns the owner at self-rank 0.
method.semanticLimit: A physical article body is the finite source unit; the review compares printed field block, core effect, explicit procedure, bounds, qualifiers, continuations and visible outcomes. Individual ordinary prose clauses were not split into a complete exhaustive sentence denominator. Exact mechanic-query execution was not replayed; title self-match and actual indexed search text are the evidence boundary.

granularityDefinition: One discovered spell article is one physical printed spell heading plus the body through the next heading, including fields, qualifiers, conditions, continuations, and article-specific tables/procedures. Shared field/class notes and the nested p.100 spell list are separate units. A body unit can be review-closed with a partial site disposition. Sentence-level prose atoms are not separately counted.

originalUnitTransfer.note: This subreport closes only the four original spell-description units. It does not replace the other PHB source reports or claim whole-book semantic completeness.

sourceDenominators.listVsDescriptionExplanation: PHB p.100 Illusionist seventh-level list contains a nested first-level Magic-user selection; the independent source roster counts 414 class-level list occurrences and 413 physical article-description heads, plus one non-article nested-list owner.
sourceDenominators.bodyProseClauseDenominator: unknown; prose was reviewed at finite article/procedure scope but not split sentence-by-sentence into a complete corpus.

visibleStructuredTablesAndOutcomeRows.detail: Owner names the table and preserves the duplicated 7th-level band and bare range glyph but supplies none of the six row values.
No dedicated rule owner displays the row multipliers or saving-throw +1/+2 footnotes; per-spell material references are not the shared grid.
Source prose maps die results 1–4 to 1–4 free rounds and 5–6 to none. Current card gives four rounds as normal but omits the six-result mapping.
The list owner contains twenty names and records the p.94 “all first-level magic-user spells” versus p.100 list mismatch.

sourceDenominators.unassessedStructuredDenominator: The list above gives explicitly counted tables/finite outcome structures recorded for this pass; inline effect descriptions that do not form a separate table are not forced into a fake row count.

discoveredUnits.label: Spell field glossary
discoveredUnits.sourceFacts: The p.43 introduction defines Range, Duration, Area of Effect, Components, Casting Time and Saving Throw, including the 10-segment melee-round / 10-round turn conversions and the meaning of negated or half effect.
discoveredUnits.ownerCheck: The PHB spell cards render field labels/values; the captured PHB rules owners contain no dedicated glossary for these field definitions.
limitations: Field label/value data exists across spell cards; this assessment concerns the shared explanatory note, not individual spell headers.
discoveredUnits.siteGap: No dedicated shared field-definition record was found; spell cards expose their own field values, but the glossary definitions/conversions are not represented as one rules unit.

sourceAssertions.siteGap: No dedicated shared field-definition record was found; spell cards expose their own field values, but the glossary definitions/conversions are not represented as one rules unit.

discoveredUnits.label: Notes Regarding Cleric Spells
discoveredUnits.sourceFacts: Source states material components are consumed at completion except standard religious items; spells/reversals may affect alignment and the reversible form must be chosen before learning; prayer does not guarantee the deity grants a spell; confidence that a deity will grant higher-level spells decreases; the referee may alter or waive components.
discoveredUnits.ownerCheck: No dedicated PHB cleric-spell-notes rule owner appears in the full 1,000-owner snapshot. Individual cards contain scattered reversal/alignment/component facts but no single record captures this note as a procedure.
limitations: This is a shared note-unit absence/partial coverage finding; it does not imply each individual card omits its own spell-specific components.
discoveredUnits.siteGap: No dedicated class-note record captures the shared component-consumption, reversal/alignment, deity-grant, or preparation caveats; individual cards may carry overlapping details.

discoveredUnits.label: Notes Regarding Druid (Cleric) Spells
discoveredUnits.sourceFacts: Source includes a four-entry component-quality grid: lesser mistletoe, borrowed mistletoe, holly and oak leaves, with separate spell-range, spell-duration and area-of-effect multipliers and +1/+2 saving-throw adjustments when a category does not apply. It defines lesser/borrowed/greater mistletoe, gives the Midsummer-Eve gold/silver-sickle harvest procedure for greater mistletoe, and specifies holly/oak collection.
discoveredUnits.ownerCheck: No dedicated PHB druid-spell-notes owner or four-entry modifier grid is present. Individual druid spell records mention mistletoe and components but do not provide the shared quality modifiers/harvesting procedure.
limitations: The independent source denominator is four material-quality rows and three effect columns plus two saving-throw footnotes; no complete atomized prose denominator is claimed.
discoveredUnits.siteGap: No dedicated record contains the four quality rows, three effect columns, two saving-throw footnotes, material definitions, and harvest/collection procedure.

findings.sourceAssertion: Duration is six melee rounds. The caster chooses a point up to six inches away, and the effect covers a five-inch square centered on that point.

siteBefore.effect: Friendly recipients gain +1 morale and +1 to hit.

findings.gap: The record drops the melee-round qualifier and does not state that the square is centered on the chosen casting point.
findings.repairCandidate: Add the two omitted spatial/time qualifiers; preserve printed source wording.

findings.sourceAssertion: The card lists the duration as permanent, then qualifies that caused wounds remain only while the creature takes no more damage; those wounds heal or can be cured like ordinary injury.
findings.gap: The card omits the source qualification that the wounds can heal/can be cured normally after the injury and that the “permanent” description is conditional on no later damage.
findings.repairCandidate: Carry the permanence/healing qualification into the rendered explanation.

findings.sourceAssertion: The barrier names a specific finite class of enchanted, conjured and summoned beings (including aerial servants, demons/devils, djinn/efreet, elementals and other named creatures), and the material procedure traces a one-foot-diameter circle.

siteBefore.effect: The barrier prevents bodily contact by the enchanted, conjured and summoned creatures described in the source.
siteBefore.material: Holy water circle, or burning incense; reverse uses blood or smoldering dung.

findings.gap: The rendered body replaces the creature list with “described in the source” and omits the circle diameter, so the rule cannot be applied from the card alone.
findings.repairCandidate: Add the named source scope and one-foot-diameter material setup.

findings.sourceAssertion: If an attacker succeeds on its saving throw, it proceeds through the ordinary attack process against the protected creature.

siteBefore.effect: Failed attacker save causes it to ignore the warded creature and attack another.

findings.gap: Only the failed-save branch is described; the normal-attack consequence on a successful save is omitted.

findings.sourceAssertion: From behind, the force hammer receives rear-attack benefit and ignores defensive adjustments such as shield protection and Dexterity.

conditions: Ends when concentration stops. If the cleric is behind an opponent, its attacks gain the rear-attack benefits described in the source.

findings.gap: The card defers the benefit to an absent source passage rather than stating the concrete defensive exclusions.
findings.repairCandidate: Replace the generic source-reference phrase with the listed rear-attack effects.

findings.sourceAssertion: The source permits ordering animated skeletons/zombies to follow or remain in a specified area and attack a creature/type that enters or is named.

effect: Animates dead human bones or bodies as skeletons or zombies that obey the cleric’s orders.

findings.gap: The owner records obedience but not the printed follow/guard-and-attack command procedure.

findings.sourceAssertion: A six-row table gives cleric-level bands, maximum time since death, questioning duration and question count.

conditions: Caster must know a language the creature used. Maximum time dead, question count and questioning duration depend on cleric level.
exceptions: PHB p.48 table places 7th level in both “up to 7th” and “7th–8th” rows. Its range header prints bare 1 without a visible unit; retain the omission without inferring a unit.

findings.gap: The card names the dependencies and source overlap but omits every row value; the 6×4 table is not rendered or indexed as table content.
findings.repairCandidate: Represent the six rows and preserve the duplicated seventh-level band and unitless printed range as source facts.

findings.sourceAssertion: The source changes the base success chance by −1 percentage point per level of difference when the cleric is lower, and +1 point cumulatively when the cleric is higher.

conditions: Once begun, interruption spoils the spell. Success is checked each turn against a random or referee-set base chance modified by relative levels.

findings.gap: The card omits the direction and signed increment of the level modifier.
findings.repairCandidate: State the signed level-difference formula; leave the referee-set base chance intact.

findings.sourceAssertion: A six-sided surprise roll yields one, two, three or four free melee rounds on 1–4, and zero on 5–6; the target’s ability to detect invisibility changes whether the normal target surprise roll is used.

conditions: Retrieval normally gains 4 free surprise rounds; a target able to detect invisibility uses the source’s surprise roll. A successful hit grabs the target, followed by a strength comparison.

findings.gap: The card gives the 4-round case and refers generically to the surprise roll but omits the six-result mapping.

findings.sourceAssertion: The source supplies movement examples tied to form/mass (e.g., light sliding and rolling objects versus heavy statues), says attack frequency ranges from once in five melee rounds to once each round, and gives damage bands by weight/material while reserving final values to the referee.

conditions: Movement, attack frequency, damage, armor class and durability depend on shape, material and mass; the referee decides these values.
Flexible objects can obstruct, trip, bind or smother; harder objects can strike or crush.

findings.gap: The card retains the referee discretion and broad categories but omits the printed movement/attack-rate/damage examples that bound those decisions.
findings.repairCandidate: Add the source’s example ranges while preserving referee adjudication of the exact object.

findings.sourceAssertion: The same paragraph says “500 gp weight cumulative per level” and gives a 15th-level example of 3,750 gp weight (375 pounds), which implies 250 gp weight per level.

conditions: May bring an additional 250 gp weight per caster level, including possessions or living companions.

findings.gap: The card selects the worked-example rate but does not disclose the contradictory printed prose rate. The source does not support silently choosing 250 or 500 as a corrected universal rule.
findings.repairCandidate: Expose both printed assertions as a source conflict; do not change the selected value without a separate ruling.
